title: The average difference between two drugs can hide large person-to-person differences
caption: For each drug pair: the average difference in daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure (first drug minus second; negative favours the first) and the estimated between-person standard deviation of that difference, both with 95% CIs, from Table 2. Aml amlodipine, Can candesartan, Lis lisinopril, HCTZ hydrochlorothiazide.
reading_note: Randomized, within-person comparisons in one trial population. A large SD next to a small average means people differ in which drug suits them; it is not a measure of anyone's personal response. The SD is a model estimate.

reference_line.label: 0 = no average difference (the SD series is non-negative by definition)
